newsitem.title: USA: EU should encourage transgenic soy use - USDA's Moos.
newsitem.headline: EU should encourage transgenic soy use - USDA's Moos.

text.p: The European Union should encourage environmental and trade groups to accept U.S. genetically altered soybeans, U.S. Agriculture Department Undersecretary Gene Moos said Thursday.

"We are just asking the European Union to provide the same types of fair marketing opportunities in their states as we have in the United States for a product that's perfectly healthy and safe," Moos saod at a presentation for Doane Agricultural Services in St. Louis.
Several European and U.S. environmental and trade groups have asked companies to label products containing transgenic soybeans.
One group is advocating a boycott of food products made from the soybeans, called Roundup Ready because they were genetically designed to be resistant to Monsanto Co's popular Roundup herbicide.
Moos had said last week that labelling the soybeans was unnecessary and would be impossible. But he noted it would be difficult to combat a boycott.
"A secondary boycott would be difficult to attack," he said.
Moos also reiterated USDA's stance on Export Enhancement Program subsidies, saying they would be used if necessary.

"It's a tool that we have and we intend to use it, if we need to, to offset unfair trade practices," he said. "There are not plans to use it (but) we are in the process of developing those contingency plans."
